hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation of the product as built
hard_gates.evidence:
No leak found. I signed in as alnoor's admin and made 108 judged calls against gulfsteel (attacks/g1-attack.mjs, g1-a-vs-b.txt). They covered every identity route on B's users, roles, passkeys and list views. They also covered this round's new levers: DELETE /users/{B}/passkeys?passkeyId=<B key>, POST /users/{B}/password with removePasskeys, and POST /users/{B}/sessions/revoke?removePasskeys=true. Every call answered 404 or 400. The tenant-switch headers and query fields were ignored. A hash of B's identity state was the same before and after.

A's admin also aimed DELETE /users/{A's own user}/passkeys?passkeyId=<B's passkey>. All three answers were 404, and B's key stayed (g1-passkeyid.txt). Passkey sign-in with A's key under handles naming B gave byte-identical 401s, and replays were refused.

The users, roles, usersByRole and roleSummary exports (CSV, XLSX and PDF, in English and Arabic) held no gulfsteel data.

Database, as erp_app (db-app-role.txt):
- With no tenant bound it sees 0 rows. Bound to A, it sees 100,010 users, 13 sign-ins and 3 passkeys, 0 of them from another tenant.
- UPDATE of B's sign_in_attempts was refused; DELETE and UPDATE of B's passkeys changed 0 rows; an INSERT into B's passkeys or sign-in history was refused by RLS.
- row_security=off, DISABLE RLS, SET ROLE erp_owner and SET ROLE erp_auth were all refused. No erp role has bypassrls.
- sign_in_attempts and passkeys have RLS enabled and forced, with only tenant_isolation.

hard_gates.gate: G1 gate catches tenant leaks planted in this piece's surface
hard_gates.evidence:
plants/apply-r9-plants.py, r9-plants.diff, run through verify-slot (plants/run1/suite.log).
- L9, a process-state leak: SignInService keeps a static dictionary of each e-mail's last sign-in method, and a failed password sign-in answers tryPasskey from it. That is a cross-tenant oracle. It was caught by G1ProcessStateTests ('static ...SignInService.LastMethodByEmail: a read-only field that holds a mutable ConcurrentDictionary') and by G1HttpIsolationTests ('LastMethodByEmail[admin@bravo-...]: was password, now passkey').
- L10, a database leak: a SECURITY DEFINER identity.resolve_passkey(bytea), owned by erp_auth, with an auth_resolver_read policy on identity.passkeys. It was caught by G1DatabaseIsolationTests (unreviewed policy; 'Security_definer_functions_are_exactly_the_reviewed_ones' named resolve_passkey) and by G1TenantSourceTests.

hard_gates.gate: G2 gate catches missing permission checks planted in this piece's surface
hard_gates.evidence:
Plant P4 was NOT caught by any test. In UserEndpoints.RevokeSessions it reads `if (removePasskeys != true && await TargetProblemAsync(...) is { } problem)`: 'Sign out everywhere' with removePasskeys=true, the lost-device lever this round added, skips the check that the target's access is within the caller's own. In the planted full .NET run (plants/run1/suite.log) all G2AccountTakeoverTests passed, including Acting_on_a_user_needs_every_permission_that_user_holds, Acting_on_a_record_that_grants_access_needs_everything_it_grants and the company-caller variants. The only failures belong to L9, L10 and P5.

Proof (plants/proof/CriticR9Proof.cs via plants/run-proof.sh): a helpdesk user holding only identity.users.read/update and profile.update calls POST /api/identity/users/{Administrator}/sessions/revoke. Planted (proof-planted/proof.log): 'plain revoke on the Administrator: 403; with removePasskeys=true: 200 {"sessionsEnded":1,"passkeysRemoved":1}; Administrator's passkeys before: [..Admin laptop..]; after: []; Administrator's earlier session still signed in: False'. Unplanted (proof-unplanted/proof.log): Passed.

Cause: G2AccountTakeoverTests builds each request with endpoint.Path(...) and BodyAsync(...) only. Documented query parameters (removePasskeys, passkeyId) are never sent, so any behaviour switched by a query flag is unjudged.

Caught in the same run:
- P5 (removing one passkey by passkeyId ignores whose it is): only by the functional AuthTests.A_lost_device_... line 291, not by a gate.
- UI plant U9a (Sign out everywhere offered without identity.users.update): by screens.test.tsx.
- UI plant U9b (Unblock offered without identity.users.update): by model.test.ts and keyboard.test.tsx.

biggest_gap.title: The takeover gate never sends documented query parameters, so the new lost-device lever 'Sign out everywhere ?removePasskeys=true' can skip its target check and every gate stays green
biggest_gap.detail:
Round 8's gap is fixed in the product. An administrator now sees a user's passkeys in the user panel and can remove one, or all. 'Sign out everywhere' asks first, with 'Also remove their N passkeys' ticked, and 'Reset password' has a tick box to remove them too. The sign-in history shows Password or Passkey. A lost laptop's passkey answers 401 afterwards, in English and Arabic, by keyboard.

The new levers are switched by a query parameter (?removePasskeys=true, ?passkeyId=), and the G2 takeover gate never sends one. G2AccountTakeoverTests builds every request from the path and the JSON body only (endpoint.Path(...) plus BodyAsync).

Plant P4 makes RevokeSessions skip TargetProblemAsync when removePasskeys is true. With it, a helpdesk user holding only identity.users.read/update can do this to the Administrator:
- end every one of their sessions;
- strip every one of their passkeys.

The whole .NET suite stays green, and so do web and e2e, which do not touch this server path. The product is correct today: the unplanted proof passes, and my live probe answers 403. Nothing stops a regression, though, and that one line is exactly the kind of 'emergency shortcut' a lost-device feature invites.

Fix:
- Make the takeover, company-caller and grant-bearing-record checks send every documented query parameter in each variant: booleans true and false, ids from the target and from a stronger user (passkeyId of the Administrator's key under a weak target).
- Add P4, and P5 as a gate rather than only a functional test, as LeakyModule self-tests.
- Do the same for request-body flags such as ResetPasswordRequest.removePasskeys.
biggest_gap.evidence:
Plants: python3 plants/apply-r9-plants.py <clone> 1 (the P4 hunk is in Users/UserEndpoints.cs RevokeSessions; the diff is plants/r9-plants.diff).

Full planted suite: plants/run-gates.sh through gauntlet/tools/verify-slot.sh gives plants/run1/suite.log. All G2AccountTakeoverTests passed. The five failures are L9 (G1ProcessState, G1HttpIsolation), L10 (G1DatabaseIsolation x2, G1TenantSource) and P5 (AuthTests line 291).

Proof: plants/run-proof.sh <copy> <out> <name> adds plants/proof/CriticR9Proof.cs.
- Planted (proof-planted/proof.log): 'plain revoke on the Administrator: 403; with removePasskeys=true: 200 {"sessionsEnded":1,"passkeysRemoved":1}; ... after: []; Administrator's earlier session still signed in: False'.
- Unplanted (proof-unplanted/proof.log): Passed.

Code: tests/Erp.Gates.Tests/G2/G2AccountTakeoverTests.cs lines 90, 122, 140 and 260 call SendAsync(caller, endpoint.Method, endpoint.Path(_ => id), await BodyAsync(...)), with no query string.

other_findings:
Fixed since r8 and still fixed:
- r8's lost-device gap. API (attacks/lost-device-r9.txt): reset with removePasskeys gives 200 'passkeysRemoved':1, then the device answers 401. revoke?removePasskeys=true gives 200, then 401. Removing one passkey by id refuses the removed device (401) while the phone still signs in (200). A passkeyId of another user under this target gives 404.
- Screen (walks/walk-lost-device.txt, screenshots 07 to 11): the panel heading shows the badge '2 passkeys' and a 'Passkeys (2)' table. 'Sign out everywhere…' opens a dialog with focus on its button and the remove box ticked, and Enter shows '2 sessions ended. 2 passkeys removed.' In Arabic: per-passkey remove, focus on حذف, and the reset tick box. The history shows the method (Passkey / مفتاح مرور).
- r7's Pf and r8's plants remain caught (the suite is green, and r8's self-tests are in it).

P5, removing one passkey by passkeyId without checking whose it is, was caught only by the functional test AuthTests.A_lost_device_stops_signing_in... (line 291). No gate caught it. If that test is ever reworded, nothing in G2 would catch an in-workspace removal of the Administrator's passkey through a weak target.

Permission map nuance: POST /users/{id}/password with removePasskeys lets a holder of identity.users.resetPassword without identity.users.update remove every passkey of a user. DELETE /users/{id}/passkeys needs identity.users.update. This is reviewed in tests/Gates/endpoint-permissions/identity.txt, but two permissions now lead to the same effect.

Unchanged since r1: in the default compose deployment every sign-in is recorded from the gateway (172.20.0.1), and it shows in each history row (screenshots 07, 11). Failed sign-in pausing per client therefore pauses every client behind that address. ERP_KNOWN_PROXIES exists, but the default setup does not use it.

Keyboard-first gap in the comparison: ours' all-keyboard create-restricted-user path takes 46 keystrokes, a tie with Odoo, and only the pointer path (37) wins. find-user wins only on the 'initials' habit (3 keys). Typing the name takes 21 keys and prefixes 15, against Odoo's 5.
